decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Leo points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Leo keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Leo a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Who invited that baby?
decisions.situation: There is a baby in the mirror. They copy every move you make. You have concerns about their manners.

choices.label: Pull your strangest face
Look behind the mirror
Wave hello

result.title: Extremely rude guest
result.body: They pull it right back. You laugh and try another one.

journal.text: I made faces at my reflection and laughed when it copied me.

decisions.title: Urgent correspondence
decisions.situation: You draw a letter and slide it into a cardboard box. It comes straight out of the missing bottom. The postal service is extremely fast.

choices.label: Fold a bottom for the box
Make a pile for each colour
Send the same letter again

result.title: Delivery delayed
result.body: The letter stays inside this time. You open the box to make sure it arrived.

journal.text: I repaired my cardboard postbox so letters would stay inside.

decisions.title: Two is more than one
decisions.situation: Your biscuit breaks in half. There are now two biscuits, although something about the total feels suspicious.

choices.label: Fit the halves back together
Celebrate the extra biscuit
Count all the little crumbs

result.title: The original arrangement
result.body: The edges match. You test them twice before accepting that both pieces were one biscuit.

journal.text: I fitted two broken biscuit halves back together.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: A nose for music
decisions.situation: Leo has learned to play the recorder with their nose. They ask you to accompany their debut. The first note makes everyone check for a trapped bird.

choices.label: Drum on the desk and let them have their moment
Offer to be the audience from further away
Announce that you can play an imaginary one

result.title: A very short tour
result.body: You find a beat that nearly matches the squeaks. Leo attempts an encore, sneezes, and announces an interval.

journal.text: I accompanied Leo’s nose-recorder debut by drumming on a desk.

decisions.title: A disappointing lunch
decisions.situation: Leo opens a lunchbox with nothing in it. They look embarrassed. Valeria is nearby.

choices.label: Quietly ask Valeria for help
Ask Leo what would help
Announce it across the table

result.title: Lunch gets sorted
result.body: Valeria helps without making an announcement. Leo looks relieved.

journal.text: I quietly got Valeria’s help when Leo had no lunch.

decisions.title: The rules have been updated
decisions.situation: You are losing a board game with Leo. You have just remembered a rule under which you would be winning.

choices.label: Finish under the original rules
Suggest your rule for the next game
Insist it has always been the rule

result.title: A respectable defeat
result.body: Leo wins this round. You immediately request another.

journal.text: I finished a board game fairly even though I was losing.

decisions.title: Forty-two. Definitely forty-two.
decisions.situation: Valeria starts a question and your hand shoots up. You have an excellent answer. You are still waiting to hear what the question is.

choices.label: Hear the rest before committing
Shout “forty-two” with total confidence
Let someone else risk it first

result.title: A useful last-minute adjustment
result.body: The question is about the number of sides on a triangle. You quietly retire forty-two and give the correct answer.

journal.text: I waited to hear a whole classroom question before answering.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Leo finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Watch it together
Ask to keep the recording private
Defend the bath theory

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Leo remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Leo.

decisions.title: Forwarded with absolutely no evidence
decisions.situation: A group chat is circulating an embarrassing rumour about someone your age. The source appears to be “everyone knows”.

choices.label: Ask whether anyone actually knows
Mute it and step away
Forward it for a reaction

result.title: An inconvenient question
result.body: Nobody produces evidence. The conversation changes topic with suspicious speed.

journal.text: I challenged a rumour in a group chat.

decisions.title: At least you know your name
decisions.situation: Your practice exam is going badly. So far, you have written your name and the date. The date is wrong.

choices.label: Hunt for every easy mark first
Take the wreckage to Sofía afterwards
Write an apology in the answer box

result.title: A rescue in small pieces
result.body: You collect enough answers to get moving. Even question one looks less hostile on your second visit.

journal.text: I recovered from freezing in a practice exam by answering easier questions first.

decisions.title: The unpaid goblin
decisions.situation: Leo turns your group presentation into a pitch for an imaginary company. You are listed as “unpaid goblin”. Their dog is CEO. Sofía asks where the actual research is.

choices.label: Open the real research before the dog gets a salary
Whisper a demand for a better job title
Delete the pitch while they are presenting it

result.title: Goblin saves the meeting
result.body: You present your actual work. Sofía marks it while Leo clicks past a slide about office beanbags. The dog receives no academic credit.

journal.text: I rescued our group presentation after Leo replaced the research with a fake company pitch.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Barcelona, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Barcelona.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing
Send someone a proper message
Investigate another hour of success

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
decisions.situation: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup
Delete the post without explaining
Add “No questions. Bring gloves.”

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: A reminder that needs reminding

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
Work backwards from the context
Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: The lost hand

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: The missing letter

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

choices.label: Ask for the whole story
Save a copy and label it
Focus entirely on the haircut

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Leo remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Leo also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Barcelona unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Barcelona.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

choices.label: Look around for a minute
Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Take a moment before answering
Say you need a short break
Deliver the sharp reply

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold
decisions.situation: At a free relaxation class, the instructor tells you to release your anger. Their phone rings. They spend the next minute shouting at a printer repair company.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about
Claim you invented motivational seminars

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
result.body: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.
